title: Table
statementMd:
Simon has a rectangular table consisting of $*n*$ rows and $*m*$ columns. Simon numbered the rows of the table from top to bottom starting from one and the columns — from left to right starting from one. We'll represent the cell on the $*x*$-th row and the $*y*$-th column as a pair of numbers $(*x*, *y*)$. The table corners are cells: $(1, 1)$, $(*n*, 1)$, $(1, *m*)$, $(*n*, *m*)$.

Simon thinks that some cells in this table are *good*. Besides, it's known that no good cell is the corner of the table.

Initially, all cells of the table are colorless. Simon wants to color all cells of his table. In one move, he can choose any good cell of table $(*x*_{1}, *y*_{1})$, an arbitrary corner of the table $(*x*_{2}, *y*_{2})$ and color all cells of the table $(*p*, *q*)$, which meet both inequations: $*min*(*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}) ≤ *p* ≤ *max*(*x*_{1}, *x*_{2})$, $*min*(*y*_{1}, *y*_{2}) ≤ *q* ≤ *max*(*y*_{1}, *y*_{2})$.

Help Simon! Find the minimum number of operations needed to color all cells of the table. Note that you can color one cell multiple times.

## Input

The first line contains exactly two integers $*n*$, $*m*$ ($3 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 50$).

Next $*n*$ lines contain the description of the table cells. Specifically, the $*i*$-th line contains $*m*$ space-separated integers $*a*_{*i*1}, *a*_{*i*2}, ..., *a*_{*im*}$. If $*a*_{*ij*}$ equals zero, then cell $(*i*, *j*)$ isn't good. Otherwise $*a*_{*ij*}$ equals one. It is guaranteed that at least one cell is good. It is guaranteed that no good cell is a corner.

## Output

Print a single number — the minimum number of operations Simon needs to carry out his idea.

## Note

In the first sample, the sequence of operations can be like this:

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/565fd475c8e83b0fe7a3c841173a550c7a5198e5.png)

- For the first time you need to choose cell $(2, 2)$ and corner $(1, 1)$.
- For the second time you need to choose cell $(2, 2)$ and corner $(3, 3)$.
- For the third time you need to choose cell $(2, 2)$ and corner $(3, 1)$.
- For the fourth time you need to choose cell $(2, 2)$ and corner $(1, 3)$.

In the second sample the sequence of operations can be like this:

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/58065713b01f09623e3d995baf698ff251d0f2ad.png)

- For the first time you need to choose cell $(3, 1)$ and corner $(4, 3)$.
- For the second time you need to choose cell $(2, 3)$ and corner $(1, 1)$.
statementZhMd:
Simon 有一张由 $*n*$ 行和 $*m*$ 列组成的矩形表格。Simon 从上到下将表格的行编号为从 1 开始，从左到右将列编号为从 1 开始。我们将第 $*x*$ 行第 $*y*$ 列的单元格表示为一对数字 $(*x*, *y*)$。表格的四个角是以下单元格：$(1, 1)$、$(*n*, 1)$、$(1, *m*)$、$(*n*, *m*)$。

Simon 认为表格中的一些单元格是*好单元格*。此外，保证没有好单元格位于表格的角上。

最初，表格中的所有单元格都是无色的。Simon 想要为表格中的所有单元格染色。一次操作中，他可以选择任意一个好单元格 $(*x*_{1}, *y*_{1})$、表格的任意一个角 $(*x*_{2}, *y*_{2})$，并为所有同时满足以下两个不等式的表格单元格 $(*p*, *q*)$ 染色：$*min*(*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}) ≤ *p* ≤ *max*(*x*_{1}, *x*_{2})$，$*min*(*y*_{1}, *y*_{2}) ≤ *q* ≤ *max*(*y*_{1}, *y*_{2})$。

请帮助 Simon！求为表格中的所有单元格染色所需的最少操作次数。注意，一个单元格可以被重复染色。

## 输入格式

第一行恰好包含两个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$（$3 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 50$）。

接下来 $*n*$ 行描述表格中的单元格。具体来说，第 $*i*$ 行包含 $*m*$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $*a*_{*i*1}, *a*_{*i*2}, ..., *a*_{*im*}$。如果 $*a*_{*ij*}$ 等于零，则单元格 $(*i*, *j*)$ 不是好单元格；否则 $*a*_{*ij*}$ 等于一。保证至少存在一个好单元格。保证没有好单元格位于表格的角上。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，即 Simon 完成目标所需的最少操作次数。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，操作顺序可以如下：

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/565fd475c8e83b0fe7a3c841173a550c7a5198e5.png)

- 第一次选择单元格 $(2, 2)$ 和角 $(1, 1)$。
- 第二次选择单元格 $(2, 2)$ 和角 $(3, 3)$。
- 第三次选择单元格 $(2, 2)$ 和角 $(3, 1)$。
- 第四次选择单元格 $(2, 2)$ 和角 $(1, 3)$。

在第二个样例中，操作顺序可以如下：

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/58065713b01f09623e3d995baf698ff251d0f2ad.png)

- 第一次选择单元格 $(3, 1)$ 和角 $(4, 3)$。
- 第二次选择单元格 $(2, 3)$ 和角 $(1, 1)$。
